title: Open-Set Recognition for Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition: A Six-Protocol Pilot Exposing Confidence Inversion Across Water Areas
content: Deployed underwater acoustic target recognition (UATR) classifiers will meet vessel types they never trained on, yet how badly standard pipelines cope lacks controlled measurement. We report a six-protocol open-set recognition (OSR) pilot on four recording-disjoint corpora: four intra-dataset class-holdout protocols plus two cross-library protocols (one corpus known, another's test classes all unknown), extending our zero-transfer finding to OSR. A ResNet-18 classifier trained with cross-entropy (CE) or the entropic open-set loss (EOS) is scored with maximum softmax probability (MSP), the energy score, and OpenMax (3 seeds). The results are sobering. The best intra-dataset protocol reaches at most 0.714 AUROC (chance 0.5). On Oceanship holdout and the QiandaoEar22→Oceanship cross-library protocol, CE+MSP falls below chance (AUROC 0.34–0.37): unknowns receive systematically higher confidence than knowns, a confidence-inversion signature of domain shift. The energy score is the only method with significant gains, zero training cost, and no significant AUROC regression (exception: a small OSCR dip on q_holdout, −0.022, p = 0.010, where MSP is best); it repairs inversion where it occurs (+0.21 AUROC, p = 0.013; +0.12 cross-library, p = 0.006). OpenMax adds two significant gains but a significant loss on VTUAD holdout (Weibull tail-fitting is unstable with few recordings per class); EOS adds none. The two ShipsEar protocols diverge: intra-dataset holdout sits at or around chance (classifier failure more than rejection quality), while Oceanship→ShipsEar cross-library is the one weak positive (CE+Energy AUROC 0.744 ± 0.095, FPR@95TPR 0.87–0.91). Which direction inverts or separates depends on the corpus pair; no method is reliable across all six.
